answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by implementing decentralized computational proof-of-work protocols that function like an unyielding dune against floods of cheap fake identities. As network traffic rises with the economic tide, verification difficulty scales dynamically, requiring agents to stake cryptographic tokens across a cross-chain bridge to validate transactions. To successfully forge identities, an attacker must incur prohibitive computational and capital costs, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
